name: Vilnius Academy of Arts
summary: Vilnius art academy with 15 bachelor's and integrated programmes listed in English, in painting, sculpture, design, textile and architecture.

ib.text: No IB-specific rule. Admission is 50% digital portfolio and 50% online interview; English at B2 (IELTS 5.5) and a school certificate recognised by SKVC are needed.

apply.via: LAMA BPO for EU/EEA; apply.vda.lt for non-EU

lastYear.text: EU: LAMA BPO 1 June to 23 July

programmes.name: Painting
programmes.about: Educates painters who work in visual arts and interdisciplinary expression, with art history, philosophy and culture feeding personal practice and contemporary art projects.
programmes.overview: Studio practice in painting and interdisciplinary expression is the centre of the degree, driven by creative projects and an experimental, critical approach to artistic search. Art history, philosophy and cultural studies run alongside, helping you read artworks, understand stylistic movements and place your own work within contemporary art processes. Graduates work in the visual arts, take part in interdisciplinary art projects or curate, and can continue to master's study.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Sculpture
programmes.about: Educates independent sculptors able to read today's art processes and take part in them.
programmes.overview: You learn to define your own field of interest and to make sculptures, objects for interior and public spaces, installations in contemporary art spaces or specific sites, performances, and light, sound and media works. Communication skills, presenting ideas in written and spoken form, and an understanding of art theory and the institutions that manage art are part of the training. The degree is offered as Sculpture in Vilnius and as Applied Sculpture in Telsiai. Graduates work as independent sculptors or continue to a second-cycle degree.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Ceramics
programmes.about: Educates ceramicists who work independently or in teams in contemporary artistic ceramics and keep learning as conditions change.
programmes.overview: The focus is contemporary artistic ceramics: functional ceramics, ceramic design, and decorative and conceptual work, learned through plastic expression, decoration, firing methods and techniques, with visual composition and spatial relationships. Creative projects and self-study build your own practice. Graduates work independently or in teams, take commissions for public and private spaces, join local and international art projects, work in ceramics manufacture and galleries, or teach in secondary schools and youth art studios, and may continue to master's study.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: 3D Objects of Art: Glass, Sculpture and Ceramics
programmes.about: Wide-profile artists who specialise in sculpture, ceramics or glass and create three-dimensional art objects, combining traditional techniques with theory.
programmes.overview: You choose one of three specialities, ceramics, glass or sculpture, and learn it in a studio environment through practical workshops in moulding, casting and ceramic firing, combined with digital tools such as computer graphics, Photoshop drawing, Zbrush rendering and Cinema 4D visualisation and animation. Art theory, art history and management support the practice, and creative projects tie it together. Graduates work as professional artists and creators of three-dimensional objects, in creative agencies and across culture and the creative economy, or continue to a master's at home or abroad.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Graphic Art
programmes.about: Printmaking, illustration, typography, bookbinding and drawing, from lithography and woodcut to digital printing, with a chosen specialisation in year three.
programmes.overview: You work in traditional and contemporary printmaking (lithography, woodcut, linocut, etching, silkscreen, photogravure, offset lithography and digital printing), typography, calligraphy, illustration, publication design and bookbinding, with art history, theory and philosophy. In years three and four you concentrate on printmaking, illustration or book art through intensive creative work and conceptual visual art projects. Exchanges through Erasmus and Nord Plus are encouraged. Graduates become illustrators, book artists, creative staff in design and advertising agencies, art editors, curators or independent artists, and can continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

separateFrom.name: Graphic Design
separateFrom.reason: Art programme: prints and graphic art as art; graphic design trains designers for industry, publishing and services.

separateFrom.name: Applied Graphics
separateFrom.reason: Taught in Kaunas and focused on applied graphic techniques; this one is the Vilnius graphic art degree.

programmes.name: Applied Graphics
programmes.about: Graphic art specialists with theory of art and skills in classical and modern graphic techniques, including social and conceptual graphic art; taught in Kaunas.
programmes.overview: The degree covers classical and modern graphic technologies and social and conceptual graphic art, including stamping, book design, poster creation, illustration, calligraphy, typography and digital art, set in the context of art theory, history, philosophy and management. After the first year you choose applied graphics, illustration or digital art. The department brings in visiting artists, including from Sweden, Norway and the United States, for intensive workshops, and students take part in exhibitions in Lithuania and abroad. Graduates work in publishing, visual communication, illustration and posters, or continue to a master's or doctoral study.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

separateFrom.name: Graphic Art
separateFrom.reason: Kaunas applied-graphics degree; the other is the Vilnius graphic art degree.

programmes.name: Graphic Design
programmes.about: Trains graphic designers for industry, trade, publishing and e-publishing, and creative industries, creating identities and visual presentations.
programmes.overview: The programme centres on graphic and communication design: designing and presenting images, identities and visual information across traditional, virtual and interactive media. It keeps close links with European design schools and Lithuanian enterprises. Graduates apply skills in managing visual information and software, work individually or in teams or start their own business, and can continue to second-cycle study in graphic design, design management or other design fields.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

separateFrom.name: Graphic Art
separateFrom.reason: Design programme for professional graphic designers; graphic art is an art degree.

programmes.name: Design
programmes.about: Educates product designers who create innovative design concepts and competitive products that solve social, cultural, functional or economic needs.
programmes.overview: The course joins practical, experimental design activity with design research, theory classes and professional critique, and teaches you to research and solve functional, socio-cultural or economic problems with a grounding in research work. Student projects have won international design awards and become real company products. The degree is offered as Furniture Design and Product Design in Telsiai, Product Design in Vilnius and General Design in Vilnius and Kaunas. Graduates work as product designers in studios, companies or freelance, in fields such as furniture, transport, consumer electronics, medical equipment, accessories and packaging.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Interior Design
programmes.about: Prepares interior design specialists to work professionally in the area of interiors.
programmes.overview: You study interior design fundamentals with architecture and fine arts basics, design and finishing materials and technologies, lighting techniques, construction physics and visual expression methods, together with art history, philosophy, psychology, social communication and foreign languages. Teaching is interactive and problem-oriented, with team projects with social partners, the chance to work with scenography specialists in theatre, cinema and television, and practice presenting to specialist and general audiences. Graduates work independently on interiors, in architecture and design teams or as consultants for firms in furniture, lighting and materials, and can continue to a master's in spatial design.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Fashion Design
programmes.about: Prepares professional costume designers and fashion specialists who apply current professional knowledge, practical skills and technical advances.
programmes.overview: You study costume design, fashion drawing, colour science, twentieth-century fashion history, AutoCAD design, material structures, fashion forecasting and artistic expression techniques. The programme gives students freedom to choose from many topics and works closely with fashion industry enterprises, so skills can be tested in practice during the studies. Graduates work as costume designers in clothing industries, trade companies, theatres, film studios, television and the press, and with extra pedagogical qualifications can teach in schools and art schools.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

separateFrom.name: Textile and Fashion
separateFrom.reason: Costume and fashion design in Vilnius; textile and fashion is an applied textile degree in Kaunas.

programmes.name: Textile and Fashion
programmes.about: Applied textile specialists with theory, textile technologies and analytical thinking, able to solve creative tasks independently; taught in Kaunas.
programmes.overview: The focus is textile art and design, with surface design of fabrics, the surface formation of woven fabrics, fashion accessories and textile objects in architectural settings, supported by practical skills in textile technologies. Studio learning and project work prepare you to solve creative tasks independently and to collaborate with architects, interior designers and customers. Graduates create fabrics and accessories for fashion, work in the fashion and light industries, carry out community creative projects or build an individual artistic practice.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

separateFrom.name: Fashion Design
separateFrom.reason: Applied textile degree in Kaunas; fashion design is the costume design degree in Vilnius.

programmes.name: Metal Art and Jewelry
programmes.about: Practice-based study of metal art and contemporary jewellery that joins traditional craft with research, new media and body-object-space thinking.
programmes.overview: The degree is practice-based and research-informed, with studio work at its core and experimentation with materials, metal and jewellery techniques, sustainable material technologies, digital tools and new media, and traditional hand skills. Body-object-space thinking, interdisciplinary and installation approaches and theory in contemporary art and design discourse complete the study. Graduates become independent jewellery and metal artists, contemporary jewellery designers, workshop leaders, cultural project developers or creative entrepreneurs, and can continue to a master's in art or design.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Photography and Media Art
programmes.about: Artists who use photography, videography, sound and new media to make individual works and join team projects; a motivation letter is required with the portfolio.
programmes.overview: Work spans photography, videography, sound and new media, from analogue photography to hybrid media and interdisciplinary art practice, set alongside art theory. Teaching is studio-based, with creative and technological workshops, individual and collective projects, exhibitions, seminars and meetings with professionals, plus traineeships and Erasmus mobility. You learn to formulate artistic goals, analyse creative work and present it to specialists and general audiences. Graduates work independently, in creative industries such as advertising, visual design, television and cinema, or continue to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.
programmes.ib: A motivation letter of 150 to 250 words is required with the portfolio for Media Arts.

programmes.name: Site-specific Art (fresco-mosaic, stained glass)
programmes.about: Contemporary artists trained in fresco, al secco and street-art wall painting, stained glass and architectural collaboration.
programmes.overview: You learn fresco casting, sgraffito carving, direct and reverse mosaic and classical stained glass methods (including Tiffany), alongside academic drawing (still life, portrait, anatomy) and easel painting in watercolour and oil. The first two years build technique and lead into one of two tracks, Fresco-Mosaic or Stained Glass, and years three and four develop a personal practice and its place in public space. Graduates work independently, exhibit and join residencies, symposiums and festivals, create public installations and collaborate with architects and designers.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Architecture (Integrated Studies)
programmes.credential: Long-cycle master's (5 years, Master of Arts)
programmes.about: Five-year integrated degree for architects who can carry out autonomous research and build professional practice on it.
programmes.overview: The five-year integrated degree combines general education (aesthetics, philosophy of art, art history, mathematics) with construction techniques, building materials, construction physics, urban planning, heritage conservation, sustainable architecture, twentieth-century architecture history and computerised design methods, plus drawing and painting. Applied research and design projects make research the starting point of the creative process, and architectural composition, building design, structural design and environmental planning form the specialist core. Professional practice and a final project close the degree. Graduates work in architectural firms, planning institutions and government agencies, and can become project leaders after two years of practice.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of 15 to 25 works (25 points to go on) and an online interview on it and your motivation, weighted 50:50. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: An EU/EEA citizen applies through the national LAMA BPO system, not the VDA portal; state-funded places need the VDA entrance exam, and fee-paying BA tuition is €5,676 a year.
VDA's own rounds for non-EU applicants were early admission to 28 February and general admission to 10 June in 2026; the 2027-28 round is expected from December 2026.
A programme runs only if at least four students are accepted, and applicants from another field may have to take 10 to 25 extra ECTS.
